newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil to outfit tanker as drill ship.
newsitem.headline: Statoil to outfit tanker as drill ship.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday one of its multipurpose shuttle tankers (MST) under construction in South Korea was to be outfitted for use as a drill ship under the name MST Odin.

The vessel will rank as the largest of its type in the world -- with storage for up to 585,000 barrels of oil -- and will be able to drill in 2,500 metres of water, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
Stavanger-based Smedvig ASA is partner to Statoil Shipping & Maritime Technology (SMT) in the project and the two will split equally total costs of about 1.6 billion crowns.
Under construction by South Korean Samsung Heavy Industries, the vessel is due for delivery in late 1997 and will be ready to drill in the summer of 1998, Statoil said.
Smedvig will outfit the MST as a drill ship in cooperation with Statoil and Norwegian offshore group Aker Maritime will supply RamRig drilling technology.
